title: Knot's spaces compose only through hubs
claim: The knot's spaces (connected non-2-colourable cubic systems) compose only through hubs. (i) Balance: every 3-edge cut of a cubic incidence graph has a point side, whose three cut edges all leave from its points, and a line side. (ii) A composition across a cut fails iff the two sides' accepted relations on the channels are disjoint. (iii) A relation on k channels whose (k-1)-place projections are full has at least 2^(k-1) states, with equality only for a parity coset (an independent set of size 2^(k-1) in the k-cube is a colour class); so two sides that both accept knots fail together only as complementary parity cosets. (iv) Across every nontrivial 3-edge cut of a knot's space the line side accepts exactly not-all-equal on its slots and the point side exactly equality on its ports, complementary halves of {0,1}^3 (point lemma of THREEFOLD-AMPLITUDE); a double cut of a knot's space accepts a twelve-class knot or no knot, and two twelve-class sides never fail together (12 + 12 > 16). So a composition of knot's spaces always meets a hub (equality fan-out), and a hub-free failing composition is a parity one. (v) The transpose of a knot's space is a knot's space (sign-nonsingularity is transpose-invariant) and exchanges the two sides of every 3-edge cut, the knot side with the hub side.
failure_conditions: A 3-edge cut of a cubic incidence graph with cut edges leaving both shores' points.
A k-channel relation with full (k-1)-projections and 2^(k-1) states that is not a parity coset.
A nontrivial 3-edge cut of a knot's space whose sides are not exactly not-all-equal and equality.
A failing join of two knot sides that is not a parity composition.
foundation_claim_scope: A structural theorem on how the knot's spaces decompose across cuts; no counting claim beyond the cited amplitudes.

validation.status: checked: balance on every 3-edge cut of four knot's spaces; side relations at every nontrivial 3-edge cut; the complementarity lemma for k <= 4 by enumeration; double cuts and cross-joins; a parity control; the transpose; no human or external review
validation.novelty: Tight cuts, the splice calculus and the point lemma are from THREEFOLD-SPACES and THREEFOLD-AMPLITUDE (on Lovász-Plummer and Robertson-Seymour-Thomas); the complementarity lemma is elementary; the reading that knot's spaces meet only through hubs and that hub-free failure is parity was found in no source checked.
